newsitem.title: USA: US House's Gingrich sees progress on spending bill.
newsitem.headline: US House's Gingrich sees progress on spending bill.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Republican leaders and White House chief of staff Leon Panetta had made good progress during Wednesday morning talks to work out an omnibus spending bill to fund the government in fiscal 1997.

"We had a very good session. We'll have a bill filed by the end of the day. Leon (Panetta) indicated he would help us get the votes and they (administration) are interested in getting this done seometime Friday or Saturday," Gingrich told reporters.

Congress must pass legislation by Oct 1 to fund federal government programs and agencies for which regular appropriations bills have not yet been approved. Republican leaders have said they are eager to avoid a repeat of last year's partial government shutdown, which was unpopular with the public.
